mainTopic: Skinning פסולי המוקדשין, letting blood from a sick בכור, and the ban on adding a מום to an already blemished animal
overview: The גמרא first asks why רב חסדא did not explain the whole ברייתא by ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון. It answers that his strict view may apply only to פסולי המוקדשין, not to a בכור. The גמרא then asks why skinning פסולי המוקדשין from the feet should be forbidden when selling them in the market is allowed for the gain of הקדש. Three answers follow: the hide's gain is the meat's loss, the act looks like working with קדשים, and there is a גזירה lest one raise herds from them. A new משנה and ברייתא then bring an argument about letting blood from a sick בכור when the cut may cause a מום. רבי יהודה forbids it, רבי מאיר allows it only in a safe spot, חכמים allow any spot but the מום does not count, and רבי שמעון lets the מום count. One teacher pairs these views with the argument about a doubtful barrel of תרומה, but the גמרא knocks down every pairing. It adds that each dispute rests on its own פסוקים. רבי יוחנן shows that the bloodletting dispute is only about adding a מום to an animal that is already blemished, read from ויקרא 22:21. The גמרא then explains how each side uses the other's words in that פסוק, and begins a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not explain the whole ברייתא by one תנא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא did not set the entire ברייתא according to ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him explain the entire ברייתא according to ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's way of explaining the ברייתא. It suggests a simpler option: put all of it in the mouth of one תנא, ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the גמרא prefers to explain a whole ברייתא by one opinion rather than split it. Since ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון seems to fit, the גמרא asks why רב חסדא did not use him for the entire text.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him establish it, meaning explain the source as following a certain view
All of it, the entire ברייתא

phrases.english: But let him establish the entire [ברייתא]
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב חסדא, who explained the ברייתא earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ כּוּלַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion before this section about how רב חסדא explained the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's explanation of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single-תנא reading is simpler, so why did רב חסדא not use one?

steps.title: His view may apply only to פסולי המוקדשין, not to a בכור
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון holds that the קדושה remains only for פסולי המוקדשין, whose sanctity is strong enough to pass to their redemption money, but not for a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון says this only there, about פסולי המוקדשין, because they are strong enough to transfer their sanctity to their redemption money. But a בכור, which is not strong enough to transfer to its redemption money, perhaps not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא could not be sure ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון fits the whole ברייתא. His rule might be limited to פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין can be redeemed, and their קדושה passes to the money, which shows a stronger sanctity. A בכור cannot be redeemed that way, so its sanctity is weaker. ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון's strict view might therefore not reach a בכור, and he cannot be used for the part of the ברייתא about a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
He only said his ruling up to this point, meaning only in that case
Consecrated animals that became blemished and disqualified
They are strong (in their level of קדושה)
To pass its sanctity onto its redemption money

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a בכור has no קדושה. It only says the בכור's sanctity is not strong enough to pass to redemption money, so its rules here may come out differently.

phrases.english: Perhaps he only said [his ruling]
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, there
only regarding disqualified consecrated animals
which are strong enough to transfer [their sanctity] to their redemption
but a firstborn
which is not strong enough to transfer [it] to its redemption
[he would] not [say so].
phrases.notes: In other words, with a בכור he might allow skinning it from the feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון's view covers every case in the ברייתא, including a בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: His view may be limited to פסולי המוקדשין, whose sanctity is stronger, so he cannot explain the בכור case.

steps.title: Doesn't ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון allow profit for the sake of הקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון's strictness. He agrees that פסולי המוקדשין are sold in the market by weight because this benefits הקדש, so why not allow skinning from the feet too?
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון hold that all פסולי המוקדשין are sold in the butchers' market and weighed by the ליטרא? This shows that since there is a gain for הקדש, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון's own position. Elsewhere we allow a more profitable way of handling פסולי המוקדשין because it helps הקדש, so why should skinning from the feet be forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed selling פסולי המוקדשין like regular meat. This is because the higher price makes people pay more to redeem them, which helps הקדש. Skinning from the feet also raises the value, so by the same logic it should be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he not hold
Butchers' market
A litra, a unit of weight
Evidently, this shows that
A gain for the Temple treasury

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, not hold
all disqualified consecrated animals
are sold in the butchers' market
phrases.notes: This is the משנה back on 31a.

phrases.english: and weighed by the litra?
Evidently, since there is a gain for the Temple treasury
he permits it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the strict ruling about פסולי המוקדשין mentioned in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון's ban on skinning פסולי המוקדשין from the feet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If benefit to הקדש allows selling in the market, the same benefit should allow the more profitable skinning.

steps.title: The gain to the hide is a loss to the meat
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא answers that skinning from the feet brings no real gain. What the hide gains, the meat loses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, said: what improves the hide damages the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question in step 3. Skinning from the feet does not actually help הקדש overall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The selling-by-weight rule was allowed because it truly brings in more money for הקדש. Here the whole hide is worth more, but the meat is damaged in the process, so there is no net gain and the reason to permit falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Improves, increases value
Damages, lowers value
Hide, skin

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said:
What improves the hide
damages the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the premise that there is a gain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Skinning from the feet is more profitable, so it helps הקדש like selling in the market.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gain to the hide is canceled out by the loss to the meat, so there is no benefit to הקדש.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל: it looks like working with קדשים
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבינא, they say in ארץ ישראל that skinning from the feet is forbidden because it looks like doing work with קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West, in the name of רבינא, they say: because he appears like one who does work with consecrated animals.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer to step 3. The problem is not money but appearance: this kind of skinning looks like a forbidden use of holy animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if there were a profit for הקדש, the act itself looks bad. Doing work with קדשים is forbidden, and this skinning resembles it, so the חכמים did not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Appears, looks like
Doing work with consecrated animals, which is forbidden

phrases.english: In the West, they say in the name of Ravina:
Because he appears
like one who performs work with consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same challenge as step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any profitable handling that helps הקדש should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: This act looks like working with קדשים, so it is forbidden regardless of profit.

steps.title: A גזירה: he may end up raising herds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין says the ban is a גזירה, lest he raise whole herds from these animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין says: it is a גזירה, lest he raise from them herds upon herds.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer to step 3. The חכמים made a protective decree so that people would not keep these animals around and breed many of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If skinning from the feet were allowed, a person might hold on to the animals to get the best price for the hides. Meanwhile they would breed into herds, which could lead to misuse of קדשים, so the חכמים forbade it as a fence.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree of the חכמים
Lest, perhaps
Herds, flocks

steps.whatToRemember: ר' אלעזר בר' שמעון forbids skinning פסולי המוקדשין from the feet, even though selling them in the market is allowed for the sake of הקדש. Three reasons are given: (1) the hide's gain is the meat's loss, (2) it looks like working with קדשים, (3) a גזירה lest one raise herds from them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin says:
It is a decree, lest he raise from them
herds upon herds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the challenge of step 3, alongside steps 4 and 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since skinning from the feet helps הקדש, it should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים forbade it as a decree so that people would not raise herds from these animals.

steps.title: The משנה: letting blood from a sick בכור
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה gives three views on letting blood from a בכור that is congested with blood: רבי יהודה forbids it, חכמים allow it without making a מום, and רבי שמעון allows it even with a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A firstborn animal that is overfilled with blood, even if it will die, may not have its blood let. These are the words of רבי יהודה. חכמים say: he may let its blood, as long as he does not make a blemish in it. If he did make a blemish, he may not slaughter it because of that blemish. רבי שמעון says: he may let its blood even if he makes a blemish in it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with an argument about whether you may cut a sick בכור to let out extra blood, since the cut could leave a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is forbidden to purposely put a מום on a בכור, because a מום lets the owner slaughter and eat it. רבי יהודה says this ban holds even to save the animal's life. חכמים allow the cut but punish a resulting מום by not letting it count. רבי שמעון allows the cut even if it leaves a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the text that opens a new section
That was gripped by blood; sick from too much blood
Letting blood: cutting the animal to release extra blood
A permanent blemish; on a בכור it permits slaughter
Firstborn male animal, holy and given to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole sugya: how far does the ban on causing a מום reach when the animal's life is at stake?

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A firstborn animal that was congested with blood,
even if it will die,
phrases.notes: He means: even if the animal will die unless the blood is let out.

phrases.english: one may not let its blood,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say: he may let the blood,
as long as he does not make a blemish in it,
and if he did make a blemish in it,
he may not slaughter it on account of that blemish.
Rabbi Shimon says: he may let the blood,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה בּוֹ מוּם.
phrases.english: even though he makes a blemish in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בְּכוֹר שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of skinning קדשים from the feet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: no bloodletting even if it will die. חכמים: allowed without making a מום, and a resulting מום cannot be used for slaughter. רבי שמעון: allowed even with a מום.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי מאיר allows bloodletting only where no blemish results
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that according to רבי מאיר, you may let blood only in a spot on the body where the cut will not leave a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A firstborn that is overfilled with blood: we let its blood in a place where it does not cause a blemish, but we do not let its blood in a place where it causes a blemish. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a fuller version of the משנה's argument. It starts with רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes the choice depend on the spot on the body. A cut in a safe spot is fine, but a cut in a spot that leaves a מום is not. This is a middle view between total ban and full permission.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place, meaning a spot on the animal's body

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the names: in the ברייתא, רבי מאיר's view sounds like the view of חכמים in the משנה. The ברייתא's חכמים go further and allow even a spot that makes a מום.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
A firstborn that was congested with blood:
one may let its blood
in a place where the cut does not make a blemish,
but one may not let its blood
in a place where the cut makes a blemish,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכוֹר שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that fills out the argument in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: bloodletting is allowed only in a spot that will not leave a מום.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: חכמים, רבי שמעון, and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds three more views. חכמים allow cutting even where a מום results, but forbid slaughter because of it. רבי שמעון allows slaughter on that מום. רבי יהודה forbids bloodletting even if the animal will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: even in a place where it makes a blemish, as long as he does not slaughter it because of that blemish. רבי שמעון says: it may even be slaughtered because of that blemish. רבי יהודה says: even if it will die, we do not let its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list, going from more lenient views to the strictest view of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are four levels. רבי יהודה allows no cut at all, רבי מאיר allows only a safe spot, and חכמים allow any spot but the מום does not count. רבי שמעון allows any spot and lets the מום count for slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as; sets a condition
Slaughtered on the basis of that very blemish
Even if it would die

steps.whatToRemember: Four levels: רבי יהודה (no cut ever), רבי מאיר (only a safe spot), חכמים (any spot, but the מום does not count), רבי שמעון (any spot, and the מום counts).

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
even in a place where it makes a blemish,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁחַט עַל אוֹתוֹ הַמּוּם.
phrases.english: as long as he does not slaughter it on account of that blemish.
Rabbi Shimon says:
it may even be slaughtered on account of that blemish.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
even if it will die,
one may not let its blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַף בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה בּוֹ מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the remaining opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: any spot is allowed, but no slaughter on that מום. רבי שמעון: slaughter on that מום is allowed. רבי יהודה: no bloodletting even to save its life.

steps.title: The same argument appears with a barrel of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר (or רבי חייא) teaches his son that the bloodletting argument matches an argument about a barrel of תרומה that may be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר taught his son, and some say רבי חייא taught his son: Just as there is an argument here, so there is an argument about a barrel of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A teacher compares our argument to a different case about תרומה. This line sets up the next step, where the גמרא quotes that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that both cases share the same idea. In both, the question is whether you must protect something holy from harm even when it can no longer be fully used. The source for the תרומה case comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like the argument here
A barrel of תרומה, produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar taught his son,
and some say it was Rabbi Chiyya who taught his son:
Just as there is an argument here,
phrases.notes: Here means the argument about letting blood from the בכור.

phrases.english: so there is an argument about a barrel of terumah,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the bloodletting argument to a parallel argument in a different area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument about bloodletting a בכור matches the argument about a barrel of תרומה.

steps.title: The משנה about the barrel of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if a barrel of תרומה may have become טמא, רבי אליעזר says you must still protect it by moving it to a hidden spot or covering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: A barrel of תרומה about which a doubt of טומאה arose. רבי אליעזר says: if it was in an exposed, unsafe place, he should put it in a hidden place. If it was uncovered, he should cover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the comparison it just made. It quotes the beginning of a משנה about a barrel of תרומה that might be טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the doubt, this תרומה may not be eaten. Still, רבי אליעזר says you must guard it from becoming surely טמא. This is like the views that still protect the בכור from a מום even when it is sick.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether it became ritually impure
An exposed, unsafe spot where impurity may reach it
A hidden, protected spot

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר in the תרומה משנה is not the same person as רבי אלעזר who taught his son in the last step. The names look alike but are different.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishnah:
phrases.notes: תרומות 8:8

phrases.english: A barrel of terumah
about which a doubt of ritual impurity arose:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
if it was in an exposed place,
he should put it in a hidden place;
if it was uncovered, he should cover it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: חָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בָּהּ סְפֵק טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source for the comparison made in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the bloodletting argument matches an argument about תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in תרומות 8:8, starting with רבי אליעזר's view that doubtful תרומה must still be guarded.

steps.title: The other two views on the doubtful barrel
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: רבי יהושע says you may leave the barrel open to טומאה, and רבן גמליאל says to change nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: if it was in a hidden spot, he may put it in an exposed spot. If it was covered, he may uncover it. רבן גמליאל says: he should not do anything new with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it started in the last step. We now have all three views on the barrel of תרומה that may be טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said to keep protecting the barrel. רבי יהושע says the opposite: you no longer need to guard it, so you may even expose it. רבן גמליאל takes a middle path: leave it exactly as it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A hidden, protected spot
An exposed spot where it can easily become טמא
He may uncover it
He should not do anything new with it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
If it was resting in a hidden place,
phrases.notes: "It" is the barrel of תרומה that may have become טמא.

phrases.english: he may put it in an exposed place;
if it was covered, he may uncover it.
Rabban Gamliel says:
He should not do anything new with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote of the משנה begun in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The comparison between the bloodletting argument and the barrel argument (step 10).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a barrel of תרומה that may be טמא: three views (רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע, רבן גמליאל).

steps.title: Matching each bloodletting view to a barrel view
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר matches רבי אליעזר, the חכמים match רבי יהושע, and רבי יהודה matches רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds like רבי אליעזר, the רבנן hold like רבי יהושע, and רבי יהודה holds like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up the three views on letting blood from a בכור with the three views on the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets blood only where no מום results, so he still protects the animal, like רבי אליעזר who protects the barrel. The רבנן allow a מום, like רבי יהושע who lets the barrel be exposed. רבי יהודה forbids bloodletting entirely, like רבן גמליאל who says to change nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים, the majority view
"Like": holds the same view as

steps.whatToRemember: Protect it = רבי מאיר / רבי אליעזר. Let it be damaged = רבנן / רבי יהושע. Do nothing = רבי יהודה / רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir is like Rabbi Eliezer,
and the Rabbis are like Rabbi Yehoshua,
and Rabbi Yehuda is like Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the full barrel משנה to spell out the comparison promised in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three bloodletting opinions follows one of the three barrel opinions.

steps.title: Maybe רבי מאיר would agree with רבי יהושע about the barrel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the match is right. רבי מאיר may be strict only because cutting the animal is a direct action. Exposing the barrel only indirectly causes טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe רבי מאיר only said his view there, because the person makes the מום with his own hands. But here, where it is only indirect, he holds like רבי יהושע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the match from the last step. It shows that רבי מאיר does not have to hold like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the בכור, the person himself cuts and makes the מום. With the barrel, he only puts it where טומאה might later reach it. Someone could be strict about directly causing damage and still be lenient about indirectly causing it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know?
Maybe
With his own hands; directly
Indirect causing

steps.confusionAlert: Here "there" (הָתָם) means the bloodletting case and "here" (הָכָא) means the barrel. In the next step these words switch.

phrases.english: From where do you know?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Maybe Rabbi Meir only said his view there,
phrases.notes: "There" is the בכור, where he allows bloodletting only without a מום.

phrases.english: since he is acting with his own hands;
but here, where it is only indirect,
he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the match from step 13, starting with רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The match of רבי מאיר to רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Direct damage (cutting the animal) and indirect damage (exposing the barrel) can have different rules.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אליעזר would agree with the רבנן about the בכור
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר may protect the barrel only because אליהו might come and declare it טהור. With the בכור, which will die if left alone, he might allow bloodletting even with a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe רבי אליעזר only said his view there, because perhaps אליהו will come and declare it טהור. But here, where the animal will die if he leaves it alone, he holds like the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues pushing back, now from the other side. רבי אליעזר also does not have to match רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Protecting the barrel makes sense because there is hope: אליהו may later rule it טהור. A sick בכור that is not treated will surely die, so even רבי אליעזר might allow a cut that makes a מום. Both sides of the comparison now look weak.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו הנביא, who will come and settle unsolved questions
And declare it טהור
Leaves alone
Dies

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison is shaky both ways. Direct and indirect damage differ, and a doubt that might be cleared up differs from an animal that will surely die.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer only said his view there,
phrases.notes: Now "there" is the barrel and "here" is the בכור, the opposite of the last step.

phrases.english: because perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure;
but here,
where if he leaves it alone it will die,
he holds like the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second pushback, now showing that רבי אליעזר does not have to match רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The match of רבי אליעזר to רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The barrel's doubt might someday be cleared up, but the בכור will surely die, so the barrel view need not carry over to the בכור.

steps.title: The רבנן may only be lenient because the animal will die
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים may allow bloodletting only because the בכור will otherwise die. With the barrel, they might agree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים may say their view only here, because if the animal is left alone it will die. But there, with the barrel, since אליהו may come and declare it טהור, they may hold like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps pushing back on the match from Step 13. It shows that the חכמים do not have to agree with רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים's leniency for the בכור may come from one special fact: the animal will surely die. The barrel has no such pressure, and there is still hope it is טהור. So they could be strict there, like רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said their view (in this specific case)
Leaves it alone
It will die
They hold

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָכָא,
phrases.english: And the Rabbis only said their view here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case of the sick בכור.

phrases.english: because if one leaves it alone, it will die;
but there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the barrel of תרומה.

phrases.english: since perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure,
they hold like Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same kind of rejection as Steps 14-15, now for the חכמים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The pairing of the חכמים with רבי יהושע
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים's leniency may depend only on the animal surely dying, which does not apply to the barrel.

steps.title: רבי יהודה may only be strict because of a direct act
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה may forbid bloodletting only because it is a direct act. With the barrel, where טומאה comes only indirectly, he might agree with רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה may say his view only here, because the person makes the blemish with his own hands. But there, where the damage is only indirect, he may hold like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now breaks the link between רבי יהודה and רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's strictness may be based on making a blemish with a direct action. Leaving a barrel open only indirectly causes טומאה, so he could be lenient there, like רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: With one's own hands, by direct action
Indirect causing

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda only said his view here,
because he is acting directly with his hands;
but there, where it is only indirect causing,
he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 16, applied to רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The pairing of רבי יהודה with רבן גמליאל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה's strictness may depend on the direct action, which is missing in the barrel case.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל may only be strict because the barrel might be pure
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל may refuse to change anything only because the barrel might turn out טהור. With a dying בכור, he might agree with the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל may say his view only there, since perhaps אליהו will come and declare it טהור. But here, where the animal will die if left alone, he may hold like the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes from the other side of the pair: רבן גמליאל does not have to agree with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the barrel, there is hope it is really טהור, so leaving things as they are makes sense. With the בכור, doing nothing means the animal surely dies, so רבן גמליאל might allow bloodletting like the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The prophet Elijah, who may one day clarify doubtful cases

steps.whatToRemember: Each pairing from Step 13 has been broken. Each תנא can be explained by a reason that fits only one of the two cases.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rabban Gamliel only said his view there,
since perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאִי שָׁבֵיק לֵיהּ מָיֵית,
phrases.english: but here, where if one leaves it alone it will die,
he holds like the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the series of rejections that began in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The pairing of רבן גמליאל with רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבן גמליאל's view may depend on the hope that the barrel is טהור, which does not apply to a dying animal.

steps.title: Each dispute is based on its own verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another reason the cases cannot be matched: each dispute comes from different פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: here they argue about verses, and there they argue about verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, more basic rejection of the whole matching idea. It sets up the next step, which will show the verses involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא showed that different reasons could apply to each case. Now it says the two disputes do not even come from shared logic. Each one rests on its own פסוקים, so matching opinions across them does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, an extra argument
They argue about verses

phrases.english: And furthermore, here they disagree about verses,
and here they disagree about verses,
phrases.notes: The second "here" points to the other case, the barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָכָא בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי וְהָכָא בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate rejection on top of Steps 14-18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole method of matching the two disputes
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each dispute rests on its own verses, not on shared reasoning.

steps.title: Leavening a מנחה that is already leavened
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that everyone agrees a person is liable for leavening a מנחה that someone else already leavened, based on two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that one who leavens after another person leavened is liable, as it says "It shall not be baked leavened" and "shall not be made."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's teaching to show how the בכור side of the debate connects to verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after a מנחה is already חמץ, more leavening still makes one liable. The verses "לא תאפה" and "לא תעשה" teach that each act of leavening counts. This shows that whether a second harmful act counts is learned from פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
One who makes something חמץ (leavened)
Liable to punishment

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
All agree about one who leavens after one who leavened,
phrases.notes: This is about a מנחה, a flour offering, that may not be made חמץ.

phrases.english: that he is liable,
as it is written: "It shall not be baked leavened" and "shall not be made."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:10 and ויקרא 2:11.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs up Step 19's claim about verses.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute is tied to verses
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching about מחמץ אחר מחמץ, from ויקרא 6:10 and 2:11

steps.title: Castrating an animal that is already castrated
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's second example: one who castrates an already-castrated animal is liable. The verse lists "נתוק" after "כרות" to teach this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about one who castrates after another person castrated, he is liable, as it says "bruised, crushed, torn, or cut." If one is liable for cutting, all the more so for tearing off! So the verse comes to include tearing off after cutting: he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's teaching with a second case. It uses the extra word in the פסוק to prove liability for a second act of damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing off is more serious than cutting, so listing it would be unneeded if it only taught a first act. The verse must therefore be teaching a new case: tearing off after the animal was already cut, which still makes one liable. This is another example of a "second act" rule learned straight from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: One who castrates an animal
Cutting
Tearing off completely
All the more so
To include (an extra case)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא's final point: the two disputes rest on separate verses, so we cannot simply pair the opinions of one with the other.

phrases.english: and about one who castrates after one who castrated, that he is liable,
as it is written: "bruised, crushed, torn, or cut,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:24.

phrases.english: If one is liable for cutting,
for tearing off, is he not all the more so liable?
Rather, it comes to include tearing off after cutting,
that he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְסָרֵס אַחֵר מְסָרֵס שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of רבי יוחנן's teaching begun in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: Liability for a second act of damage, learned from verses
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:24, read with a כל שכן argument

steps.title: The real dispute: adding a blemish to a blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר and the רבנן disagree only about causing a blemish in an animal that is already blemished. Each side has its own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about someone who makes a blemish in an animal that already has a blemish. רבי מאיר holds by the words 'no blemish shall be in it.' The רבנן hold by the words 'it shall be perfect to be accepted.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his teaching by pointing to the one case where there really is a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'any blemish' as a total ban, so even an animal that is already blemished may not be given another blemish. The רבנן read 'perfect' as the condition: the ban covers only an animal that is still perfect and fit for the מזבח. Both opinions come from the same פסוק, ויקרא 22:21.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who causes a blemish in a קדשים animal
An animal that already has a blemish
'It shall be perfect to be accepted', the first half of the פסוק
'There shall be no blemish in it', the second half of the פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the dispute is not about whether causing a blemish is forbidden. It is only about whether the ban still applies once the animal is already blemished.

phrases.english: They disagreed only
about one who causes a blemish in an animal that is already blemished,
for רבי מאיר holds:
"There shall be no blemish in it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:21. רבי מאיר reads 'כל' (any) as covering every case, even an animal that is already blemished.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold:
"It shall be perfect to be accepted."
phrases.notes: This is the first half of the same פסוק. To the רבנן, the ban only protects an animal that is still perfect.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּמֵטִיל מוּם בְּבַעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוחנן's teaching by naming the one case that is actually in dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids causing a blemish in an already blemished animal. The רבנן permit it.
steps.whatToRemember: The bloodletting dispute rests on how to read ויקרא 22:21 ('כל מום לא יהיה בו' against 'תמים יהיה לרצון'). The תרומה barrel dispute does not rest on that פסוק. This is why the גמרא in step 19 said we cannot pair the opinions of one dispute with the other.

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר read 'perfect to be accepted'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר learns from the words the רבנן rely on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what does he do with the words 'it shall be perfect to be accepted'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next move. Since רבי מאיר does not use these words like the רבנן do, what does he learn from them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. If רבי מאיר does not use 'perfect' to limit the ban, he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? In other words, what does he learn from this פסוק?

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר,
this phrase "It shall be perfect to be accepted",
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הַאי תָּמִים יִהְיֶה לְרָצוֹן מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי מאיר reads the פסוק the רבנן relied on in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי מאיר learns from 'תמים יהיה לרצון'.

steps.title: First answer: to exclude an animal born with a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי מאיר uses the words to exclude an animal that was blemished from the very start.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to exclude an animal that had a blemish from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer. According to רבי מאיר, the words exclude only an animal that was blemished from birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, רבי מאיר makes a distinction. An animal that was once perfect and later got a blemish may not be given another one. An animal that was blemished from the start may be.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude a case from a rule
From the start

phrases.english: He needs it
to exclude an animal that was blemished from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words exclude an animal that was blemished from birth.

steps.title: That is obvious: a born-blemished animal is like a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer. An animal blemished from birth never became holy for the מזבח, so no פסוק is needed to exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal blemished from the start? That's obvious! It is just like a palm tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 24 by saying that such a פסוק would be teaching something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born with a blemish can never become a קרבן. It is no more holy than a tree, so of course the ban on causing a blemish does not apply to it. A פסוק would not be needed to teach this.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious, so why would a source be needed?
A palm tree

phrases.english: An animal blemished from the start?
That's obvious,
it is merely a palm tree!
phrases.notes: He means that, as far as the מזבח goes, the animal has no more holiness than a tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ פְּשִׁיטָא דִּיקְלָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'תמים יהיה לרצון' excludes an animal blemished from birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק is not needed to teach something obvious, and an animal blemished from birth never had the holiness of a קרבן.

steps.title: Final answer: to exclude disqualified קדשים after redemption
steps.stepSummary: The words teach that once disqualified קדשים are redeemed, there is no ban on blemishing them. Without the פסוק we might have thought there was, since shearing them and working with them stay forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to exclude disqualified קדשים after they are redeemed. I might have thought: since they stay forbidden for shearing and work, they should also be forbidden for blemishing. The פסוק teaches us that they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for how רבי מאיר uses the words 'perfect to be accepted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeemed פסולי המוקדשין still keep some limits: you may not shear them or work with them. So one might think the ban on causing a blemish also stays. The word 'perfect' teaches that once they are redeemed, the ban on blemishing no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: קדשים animals that became unfit for the מזבח because of a blemish
Redemption, which moves the holiness onto money
Shearing and working with the animal
It could have entered your mind to say (I might have thought)
It teaches us that it is not so

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר forbids adding a blemish to a קדשים animal that is already blemished. But once disqualified קדשים are redeemed, the ban is gone, even though shearing them and working with them stay forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Redeemed פסולי המוקדשין are not fully regular animals. Shearing them and working with them are still forbidden. Only the ban on causing a blemish falls away.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to exclude
disqualified consecrated animals after their redemption,
for it would enter your mind to say:
since they are forbidden for shearing and for work,
let them also be forbidden regarding blemishes,
so it teaches us that they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַעוֹטֵי פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 25 rejected with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since redeemed disqualified קדשים are still forbidden for shearing and work, they should also be forbidden for blemishing.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, 'תמים יהיה לרצון' teaches that the ban on causing a blemish does not apply after redemption.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with רבי מאיר's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן. The פסוק 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' seems to forbid blemishing even an animal that is already blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן too: isn't it written, 'There shall not be any blemish in it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question around. It asks the רבנן how they handle the פסוק that רבי מאיר uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'כל מום' as forbidding even an extra blemish on an animal that already has one. If that is what the פסוק means, the רבנן would seem to be ignoring it. So the רבנן must use these words for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And the רבנן also (the reverse question)
But isn't it written?
Any blemish

phrases.english: And the Rabbis as well,
isn't it written: "There shall not be any blemish in it"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:21. This is the פסוק רבי מאיר relies on.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 23. Step 23 asked how רבי מאיר uses the רבנן's words; now the גמרא asks how the רבנן use רבי מאיר's words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן that blemishing an already-blemished animal is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' seem to forbid every blemish. So the רבנן must account for them.

steps.title: The verse teaches that indirect blemishing is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, the פסוק comes to forbid causing a blemish even indirectly.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק comes to teach about an indirect action (גרמא).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן. They use 'כל מום לא יהיה בו' for a different lesson: you may not cause a blemish even indirectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree the פסוק adds something. It just adds a different thing than רבי מאיר says. For them, it adds the way the blemish is caused (indirectly, through גרמא), not the kind of animal (one that is already blemished).

keyTerms.meaning: Indirect causing: setting things up so the damage happens on its own
It comes to teach

phrases.english: It comes to teach about an indirect action,
phrases.notes: He means blemishing the animal in a roundabout way, not by doing it with your own hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִגְרָמָא הוּא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the רבנן ignore the extra words 'כל מום'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן use these words to forbid causing a blemish indirectly (גרמא).

steps.title: A ברייתא that learns the indirect blemish from the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that uses this פסוק. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'There shall not be any blemish in it.' From here I only know...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its answer. This line only opens the ברייתא and sets up the rest of it, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא starts with the basic case the פסוק clearly covers. Then, in the part still to come, it will show how the פסוק also covers an indirect blemish. That will support the answer in step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (the first part of a 'from here I only know X; how do I know Y?' pattern)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: "There shall not be any blemish in it"
— from here I have derived only
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here. The ברייתא finishes it on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That 'מום לא יהיה בו' teaches the ban on an indirectly caused blemish
